originalTitle: Huge crowds watch attempt to rescue shark stranded in South Korean canal
summary: Early on Thursday morning local time, South Korea's oceans ministry said the shark had been successfully guided out of the canal.
content:
Huge crowds have flocked to a canal in South Korea to watch a stranded shark.

The 9ft 10in (3m) shark, nicknamed Bukangi, was first spotted in the waterway last month in the south-eastern city of Busan.

Early on Thursday morning local time, South Korea's oceans ministry said the shark had been successfully guided out of the canal.

It is thought the shark may have been drawn to the canal by unusually warm water and plenty of fish.

The BBC's Seoul correspondent Jake Kwon goes to Busan to follow the latest attempt to rescue Bukangi, who has since been successfully guided out of the canal.

Video edited by Marina Costa, filmed by Hosu Lee.
chineseTitle: 大批民众围观韩国运河困局鲨鱼救援行动
chineseSummary: 当地时间周四凌晨，韩国海洋部表示，鲨鱼已被成功引导出运河。
chineseContent:
大量人群涌向韩国的一条运河，观看搁浅的鲨鱼。

这条9英尺10英寸（3m）的鲨鱼，绰号Bukangi，上个月首次在东南部城市釜山的水道中被发现。

当地时间周四凌晨，韩国海洋部表示，鲨鱼已被成功引导出运河。

人们认为鲨鱼可能是被异常温暖的水和大量的鱼吸引到运河的。

BBC 驻首尔记者 Jake Kwon 前往釜山，追踪营救 Bukangi 的最新尝试，目前 Bukangi 已被成功引导出运河。

视频由 Marina Costa 编辑，由 Hosu Lee 拍摄。
whyItMatters: 这条信息属于全球新闻信号，适合用于观察外部环境、政策变化、地缘风险和市场情绪。
